experiment: T01: scripted Playwright vs an agent-driven CDP browser harness
question: For scripted browsing tasks, is a raw Playwright script better than a model driving a browser harness?

armA_browser_exec.note: fill_input+form.submit sent empty value twice; JS value-set worked

armB_playwright.note: wait_for_selector was slow on the separate machine

notes: Arm A: an existing CDP browser harness driven by the default model, which writes selectors live (model turns were not metered separately). Arm B: raw Playwright 1.5x on a separate machine with Chromium, zero model tokens per run once the script exists. Outputs were identical on all three tasks. The main difference is not speed but who writes the selectors: the model each time (with retries), or a person once.
finding: Split by stability: fixed, repeatable jobs suit a scripted Playwright job; exploratory, login-walled or one-off jobs suit the agent harness.
followups: Re-run T3 with longer timeout to separate load time from tool time
Test arm B against a bot-walled page (the harness's real edge case)
